top_choice_rationale: Anne Carson (P001) remains my first choice on the literary merits. Judged from public knowledge rather than fresh reading, her voice is distinctive and her formal achievement is real: Autobiography of Red recasts a fragmentary source as a modern verse novel, Nox makes elegy a book whose form is part of the mourning, and the essays, including Eros the Bittersweet, belong to the same practice. That practice is to rework an inherited or broken form until it carries an argument about grief and desire, and it runs across several decades. I would credit only the original poetry, verse narrative and essays, with the translations and versions as context. English removes one translation uncertainty but adds no merit. Real reservations remain: the case is clearest in a handful of titles, I cannot verify that the later and more performance-oriented books sustain that level, and a text-only reading understates Nox. P002 (Cărtărescu) is a close and defensible second. His single project at large scale is easier to state, and I cannot judge his Romanian prose or the sustained quality of the long novels directly. I weigh compressed lyric invention and formal economy slightly above large-scale architecture, and I hold that weighting with uncertainty. Opening or round-1 support counts are not evidence of merit. Either named writer is preferable to no award, since both oeuvres show sustained quality and depth, so P000 is last.
